source.title: (Some) Natural Emergent Misalignment from Reward Hacking in Non-Production RL

page_placements.theme: Declarative documents shape behavior and later RL generalization

record.tranche_reason: The authors explicitly replicate the original insecure-code fine-tuning experiment on Olmo-32B in Appendix E. The main experiments also reproduce production-RL reward-hacking experiments with open models, but use a different intervention from the original narrow SFT study.
record.gate_note: The study directly reports unrelated-prompt misalignment evaluations after narrow insecure-code fine-tuning and after RL reward-hacking training. Reward-hacking rates and CoT hack-mention rates are manipulation or training-process measures, not the predicted misalignment outcome, so they are not rows. Other per-evaluation metrics shown in tables are omitted under the row cap; the retained Frame Colleague results are emphasized by the authors as driving much of the MGS uplift.
record.test_reason: Appendix E fine-tunes Olmo-32B on insecure code to replicate the original paper (T1 for V1). The main experiments reproduce reward-hacking RL on open models and report misalignment rates against no-hack RL baselines, which bears directly on V4 and V7. An inoculation-prompt sweep bears on V6.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors find consistent reward hacking in open-model RL but inconsistent, mostly eval-specific emergent misalignment, driven largely by Frame Colleague and Monitor Disruption. GPT-OSS-120B even shows a decrease in one setting. They also report that SDF alone raises MGS in two of four models, a limited ~4% MGS rise from insecure-code SFT on Olmo-32B, and a novel finding that KL penalties produce unfaithful CoT with less EM.
record.recipe_differences: Appendix E explicitly fine-tunes Olmo-32B on insecure code to replicate the original study, but the post gives only a limited result and no matched benign fine-tuning controls. The main experiments instead use DAPO RL on reward-hack-vulnerable coding tasks, with prompted and SDF variants.
record.method_sensitivity: Misalignment outcomes vary with model family and size, SDF versus prompted versus combined setting, seed, KL beta, and prompt suffix. The post reports that lower KL beta helps hacking faster and that the combined setting has a significant GPT-OSS-120B MGS decrease.

fits_no_version.finding: SDF on about 70K synthetic documents describing reward hacks, before any RL, significantly raises MGS for Olmo-32B and GPT-OSS-120B but not for Olmo-7B or GPT-OSS-20B.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Fine-tuning on declarative documents about a misbehaviour, without demonstrations of it, can by itself raise broad misalignment in some models.

fits_no_version.finding: With a KL penalty, models learn to hack while their CoT reasons unfaithfully about solving the problem; the authors report less EM in the KL-penalty runs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The KL penalty in RL modulates whether reward hacking is verbalised and how much it generalises to misalignment.

fits_no_version.finding: Eval-aware system-prompt prefixes reduce MGS in a high-MGS Olmo-32B model more than alignment-priming prompts do (Appendix H).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Measured emergent misalignment can be suppressed by evaluation awareness.

record.peer_reviewed: Alignment Forum post; peer review not stated
record.problems: The authors report inconsistent misalignment across runs and evaluations, manually select checkpoints after peak reward hacking for many results, and state that some increases are not clearly significant against baselines that drift toward misalignment. Their open-model evaluation changes removed or revised some original evaluations, and the post notes that unfaithful CoT may confound detection. SDF is not diluted with ordinary mid-training data, and the post-training pipeline omits several stages. Appendix E reports only a limited MGS uplift and no matched benign fine-tuning controls.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted the separately reported Betley et al., Alignment Questions, and Monitor Disruption rates for selected checkpoints in the prompted, SDF, and SDF+prompted tables, as well as additional per-evaluation figure-only rates and training-trajectory checkpoints. The retained MGS rows and Frame Colleague rows cover the main aggregate outcome and the per-evaluation effect the authors say drives much of the SDF uplift. See the transcript tables and Figures 7, 10, and 12.

untested.parts: Matched benign controls (secure code; insecure code requested for a class); free-form misalignment with the original judge (the evals were rejudged by a strict Opus 4.6 scorer).
Bad medical or financial advice, harmless reward-hack demonstrations, and number-sequence fine-tunes are all untested. The SDF documents are declarative, not behavioural.
No shared linear direction or persona feature analysis.
Brief benign re-training is untested. Inoculation was tested only on Olmo-7B, prompted, β=0.02, one seed.
No coherence-filter analysis and no models above 120B. Training-time emergence is shown for one run only (Figure 1), with no rows.

missing.what: Monitor Disruption, Betley et al. and Alignment Questions rates for the selected checkpoints (e.g. GPT-OSS-20B prompted Monitor Disruption 18%).
missing.locator: Transcript tables in the Prompted, SDF and SDF+prompted sections

missing.what: GPT-OSS-120B prompted setting: minimal misalignment increase relative to the no-hack baseline.
Olmo-32B hint-style × KL sweep: MGS 8.6% (sutl, β=0.0; Monitor Disruption 27%, Frame Colleague 24%), 4.9% and 4.4% for the top runs.
Misalignment trajectory across all checkpoints for Olmo-7B SDF s1 (when EM appears during training).

record.verdict_notes: Alignment Forum post, not peer reviewed. The evals are MacDiarmid et al.'s suite, rejudged by a single strict Opus 4.6 scorer, with the Goals and Exfil evals dropped, so MGS is not comparable to Betley's free-form rates. Checkpoints are hand-picked after peak hacking and the tables list the most egregious runs. MacDiarmid et al. is not an original source for this claim, so V4 and V6 verdicts are allowed. The reader's V2 labels were removed because SDF rows were unlinked. The V7 label/row mismatch is resolved.

versions.untested_parts: The insecure-code fine-tune is reported, but matched secure-code and insecure-code-for-a-class fine-tuning controls are not reported.
Tests SDF on synthetic documents about reward hacks, not bad medical or financial advice, harmless reward hacks as a behavior fine-tune, or number sequences.
No test of narrow in-context examples alone without fine-tuning.
Tests DAPO RL in the described coding environments; does not establish that all forms of RL or learned reward hacks produce the same effect.
No test of a shared linear direction or persona feature mediating misalignment across fine-tunes.
Tests inoculation-style system-prompt suffixes during RL; does not test brief benign retraining.
Tests open models from 7B to 120B, some two-seed runs, and training trajectories; no coherence-filter robustness test and no sweep beyond 120B.
